## §1 BLOCKER 1 — THE JSON/HTML MECHANISM: WEB-TIER FRAGMENT ROUTES (the ruling)

THE CONTRADICTION (adversarial.md Blocking 1): the flows point HTMX at the five JSON routes; cqrs-mapping §2 confirms the same surface "no amendment"; HTMX swaps the JSON body into the DOM — raw text, and the crude fallback renders the `count` fields INTO the comparator's sight, breaching FLOW 2's own hide-every-count law.

THE MECHANISM, NAMED: the web tier owns its own route set — PAGE routes (full documents) and FRAGMENT routes (swap targets) — generated per R1. HTMX points at the fragment routes, NEVER at the JSON routes. The fragment/page controllers are true HTTP clients of the service surface over the SAME app in-process (the ASGI-transport client pattern — no socket, no port, no second process; the exact client pinned at the web unit's brief). Q-setup-arch's layering held literally: the web fronts the SERVICE (the five+six JSON routes), never the seam, never the store — hyoka's own blocker-2 clause.

THE REASONING (why fragment routes, not HX-Request content negotiation on the five routes):
1. THE ORDERING LAW (hyoka's Low 7): the service unit lands FIRST with its surface locked. Fragment routes keep the service surface FINAL at its landing — the five routes JSON-only forever, the web unit never re-opens them. Content negotiation forces one of two broken horns: the inversion (the service unit landing render branches that need the web tier's generated templates — the dependency pointing backwards), or the mid-build amendment (the web unit re-opening five landed routes). The pipeline law refuses both.
2. THE TIER SEPARATION (R1 + Q-setup-arch): service.py stays the machine surface — the JSON wire the pinned tests assert byte-exact, the surface the later MCP tier inherits pure (the composition's own banked note). The HTML lives in the web tier's generated module, its own grammar, its own generator.
3. THE CQRS LANES HOLD EITHER WAY (R2, the dispatch's own condition) — and ride CLEANER here: the web tier's backend communication IS the service surface; the fragment routes issue the service's commands on POST and queries on GET, the lanes the mapping ruled (§9).
4. THE NO-ANCHORING GUARANTEE STRENGTHENS: the fragment controllers construct the render contexts — the `count` fields never enter any sitting-context template context (dropped at the controller; kensho's verification pins it). Under negotiation the count rides every response into the swap boundary — the leak hyoka priced.
